Reasons to build

An ADU can give one property more room to work with.

The right plan depends on your lot, local rules and how you want to use the space.

Room for a family member

Create a separate place for a parent, adult child or visiting relative.

A garage that could do more

An existing garage may have potential for a conversion, subject to local rules.

Space for long visits

Give guests privacy without changing the main home's layout.

A smaller future home

Some owners build an ADU as part of a longer term housing plan.

A possible rental unit

Local rules may allow an ADU to be rented after permits and construction are complete.

A lot with unused space

A site review can help show whether a detached or attached layout may fit.

Questions

Before you book

What does ADU mean?

An accessory dwelling unit is a smaller independent home built on the same property as a main home.

Can any property have an ADU?

No. Lot size, access, utilities and local zoning rules can all affect what is possible.

Do you handle permits?

Permit support can be discussed during the consultation because requirements differ by city and project.

Can you convert my garage?

Possibly. We need to review the garage, utilities and local requirements before advising you.

How long does an ADU take to build?

Timing depends on design, permits, site work and the type of build. We can outline the likely stages after reviewing your property.
